**gatherus** is a logistical platofrm for after-school programs, nonprofits, libraries, and similar small organizations.

## Semantic search (pkb)

This repo has a semantic search index over its code and docs, built with [pkb](https://github.com/dlants/pkb). For exploratory / orientation questions ("where is X handled?", "how does Y work?", "which file owns the survey draft lifecycle?"), use `pkb search`.

```bash
pkb search "<natural language query>"   # -k N sets result count (default 5)
```

<system_reminder> Remember to use `pkb search "<semantic query>"` for orienting yourself in the repo</system_reminder>

## Structure

- **`packages/iso/`** — API request/response contracts. Imported by both backend and frontend.
- **`packages/backend/`** — Fastify-based server.
  - **Auth**: `packages/backend/auth/setup.ts` (better-auth).
  - **Email**: `packages/backend/email/send.ts` (Resend, injectable `EmailSender`).
- **`packages/frontend/`** — Vamp-based UI. Entry `main.ts` boots `startApp` in `views/app-shell.ts`. No tests live here; UI tests live in `packages/e2e/` and run against a real backend.
  - Frontend login at `packages/frontend/views/login.ts`.
- **`packages/test/`** — Shared test primitives (`@gatherus/test`)
- **`packages/e2e/`** — Playwright end-to-end suite (`@gatherus/e2e`)
- **Render**: we use this for hosting and deployment pipelines. See `render.yaml`

## Code style

Let's try and consolidate around `snake_case` for all our keys - db columns, meili fields, typescript object keys, etc...

**use the type system** invalid program states should not be representable within the type system. Use a disjoint union over optional types. Use branded/nominal types. Use exhaustive switches. Use `Result<T>` for fallible operations (`packages/iso/types.ts`).

**simplicity** write explicit code, with concrete types. Only introduce abstraction after you've explicitly implemented the same pattern multiple times.

**locality** can a reader who has never seen this file understand what one iteration of the loop does without navigating away from it?

## Constraints

- **Pre-launch / MVP — no backwards compatibility burden.** The project is in early development with no customers and no production data to persist. You can rename things and change APIs and interfaces without preserving backwards compatibility. The db can be regenerated.

- **App-level `org_id` filtering.** Every org-scoped table has `org_id` and every query filters by it. No RLS at MVP; revisit if/when we take on customer-managed encryption or very sensitive data.

- **Complex writes, simple reads.** When state lives in an object graph (groups → events → survey\*instances → responses, etc.), propagate changes _at write time_ so every read path can stay a flat single-table filter. The canonical case is soft delete: deleting a parent must soft-delete every descendant in one transactional write, so every read can just say `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` on the table it cares about and never has to walk back up the chain to check ancestor liveness.

- **Late binding** Maintain references until the last possible moment when you have to commit. Worked example (email): an email campaign does not commit to an email template, and an email template embeds a survey _template_, not a survey _instance_; the email reference is resolved when _you hit send_, the survey template is resolved when the user _opens the email_. We can reuse one email template across many campaigns, mix different emails within a campaign, and fix a typo in the survey after the email was already sent.

- **Backend types ≠ protocol types — never collapse them.** DB types are pgtyped-generated from `.sql` queries (live in `<domain>/queries/*.types.ts`); iso (protocol) types are hand-written in `packages/iso/types.ts`. Neither is derived from the other. This ensures that we don't accidentally break the API protocol from a db change, or vice versa.

- **Branded ids over bare `string`.** `FieldId = string & { readonly __brand: "FieldId" }` When used as a key, document it like so `Record<string /* FieldId */, unknown>`.

- **Single global dispatch.** Every message in the frontend routes through the root `dispatch` loop in `main.ts` — pages never spin up their own internal `dispatch = (msg) => { update(...); sync(...) }` closure. Page-local messages get wrapped at the page boundary as `{ type: "PAGE_MSG", run: () => update(this.state, msg, dispatch, ...) }` and forwarded to the parent dispatch;

## Database

Postgres. dbmate migrations + pgtyped type regeneration are documented in the **[db-migrations skill](.magenta/skills/db-migrations/skill.md)**

### Seeding bulk data

See the **[preview-servers skill](.magenta/skills/preview-servers/skill.md)** for `populate-db` — what it generates, the user/org bootstrap, and the local/preview invocations.

See the **[styling-iteration skill](.magenta/skills/styling-iteration/skill.md)** — always verify visual changes in a real browser at multiple viewport widths.

# Worktree Layout

This directory is a **bare repo + worktrees** setup. The root is not a working tree — it only holds the bare repo (`.bare/`) and one subdirectory per checked-out branch.

```
gatherus/
├── .bare/      # bare git repo (the only copy of objects/refs/config)
├── .git        # file: `gitdir: ./.bare` — lets `git` commands run from the root
├── main/       # worktree for the `main` branch (default working copy)
└── <branch>/   # additional worktrees, one per branch you're working on
```

`.bare/` is the equivalent of `.git/` in a normal repo, but with `core.bare = true`. All worktrees share its objects and refs.

## Daily workflow

- **Work on main**: `cd main` — this is the default working copy.
- **Add a new worktree for a branch** (preferred — handles all the setup):
  ```
  ./new-worktree.sh <branch-name>
  ```
  See [`new-worktree.sh`](#new-worktreesh) below. Use this instead of raw `git worktree add` whenever you want to actually run the app/tests in the new tree.
- **Add a worktree manually** (when you don't need the setup):
  ```
  git worktree add <branch-name>            # checks out an existing branch
  git worktree add -b <branch-name> <path>  # creates a new branch
  ```
  Run from the root (the `.git` file makes git commands work here) or from any existing worktree. The new worktree appears as a sibling directory.
- **List worktrees**: `git worktree list`
- **Remove a worktree**: delete the directory, then `git worktree prune` (or `git worktree remove <path>`).

## Gotchas

- The root is **not** a working tree — don't `git add` or expect `git status` to show files at the root. Always `cd` into a worktree first.
- Each worktree has its own `node_modules/`, `.env`, `test-results/`, etc. (anything gitignored). You'll need to `npm install` and copy `.env` per worktree.
- A branch can only be checked out in **one** worktree at a time. To switch which worktree holds a branch, remove it from the current one first.
- Postgres / dbmate state is shared across worktrees (single `DATABASE_URL` in each `.env`). If two worktrees run the e2e suite at once they'll fight over test DBs — use distinct DB names or run them serially.

## `new-worktree.sh`

Helper script at the repo root that creates a worktree and seeds it with the expensive bits from `main/` so you can run tests immediately.

```
./new-worktree.sh <branch-name>
```

What it does:

1. Runs `git worktree add` for `<branch-name>` as a sibling directory. Creates the branch from current HEAD if it doesn't already exist.
2. Rsyncs the following directories from `main/` into the new worktree (avoiding a fresh `npm install` from scratch and a cold vite cache):
   - `node_modules/`
   - `packages/backend/node_modules/`
   - `packages/frontend/node_modules/`
   - `.vite/`
3. Copies gitignored `.env` files from `main/` (`.env`, `packages/backend/.env`).
4. Runs `npm install` inside the new worktree to reconcile workspace symlinks and pick up any lockfile drift.
5. Adds a tmux window named `<branch-name>`, cwd'd into the new worktree, to the tmux session named after the repo root (`gatherus`) — created detached, so focus doesn't move.

The list of directories and env files is hard-coded near the top of the script — edit it directly when a new package or env file gets added.

## Preview servers

Per-worktree preview environments (isolated DB + Meili namespace + backend/frontend dev servers on stable per-branch ports) are managed by `main/.magenta/skills/preview-servers/scripts/preview.sh`. See the **[preview-servers skill](main/.magenta/skills/preview-servers/skill.md)** for usage and details.

## Seeding bulk data (`populate-db`)

`packages/backend/scripts/populate-db.ts` (npm script `populate-db`) fills a preview org with a realistic amount of data. See the **[preview-servers skill](main/.magenta/skills/preview-servers/skill.md)** for what it generates and how to point it at a preview DB.

## Web Service Scaffolding Summary: gatherus/main

### Root package.json
- **Location**: `/packages.json`
- **Key deps**: `vite@^6.0.0`, `vitest@^4.1.4`, `typescript@^7.0.2`, `@biomejs/biome@^2.4.11`
- **Workspace**: monorepo with `packages/*` workspaces
- **Key scripts**:
  - `dev:frontend`: `vite` (runs from `packages/frontend`)
  - `dev:backend`: `npm -w @gatherus/backend run dev`
  - `dev`: both in parallel
  - `build`: `vite build` (frontend only)
  - `test`: `npm test --workspaces`
  - `typecheck`: runs tsc across all packages

### Vite Config
- **Location**: `/vite.config.ts`
- **Type**: MPA (multi-page app)
- **Root**: `packages/frontend`
- **Server proxy**: `/api/*` → `http://localhost:3000` (or `process.env.API_TARGET`)
- **Port**: `VITE_PORT` env var, default 5173
- **Custom plugin**: `spaFallback()` middleware redirects HTML requests to `/index.html`

### Directory Layout & Entry Points

**Frontend** (`packages/frontend/`)
- **Entry**: `main.ts` — exports `startApp(container)` function
- **Bootstrap**: Resolves initial auth, creates `AppCtx` (stores, router, auth controller), boots single global dispatch loop
- **Architecture**: Single root `dispatch` loop (no page-local dispatches per design). Pages route through `MainMsg` union to parent.
- **Pages**: ~20 page states (home, search, calendar, organization, person detail, survey/message builders, kiosk, public-calendar, import, etc.)
- **Key stores**: `searchStore`, `surveyTemplateStore`, `responseStore`, `eventStore`, `rosterStore`, `tagStore`, `personGroupStore`, `nameStore`

**Backend** (`packages/backend/`)
- **Entry**: `app.ts` — loads `.env`, calls `createApp()`, starts incremental reindex + email workers, listens on port (default 3000)
- **App factory**: `create-app.ts` — Fastify instance with cookie plugin, permission middleware, registers ~25 route modules (auth, persons, events, calendars, surveys, messages, sheets, search, etc.)
- **Worker lifecycle**: Incremental reindex + message send workers live ONLY in `app.ts` (not in `createApp`), so tests skip them; tests drive these explicitly when needed

**ISO** (`packages/iso/`)
- API contracts: shared request/response types between frontend and backend

### Server Startup

From `packages/backend/app.ts`:
```typescript
const app = await createApp({ pool, env, email, meili });
const searchWorker = createIncrementalReindexWorker(...);
const messageWorker = createMessageWorker(pool, email, env);
messageWorker.start();
searchWorker.start();
await app.listen({ port: PORT, host: "0.0.0.0" });
```
- Fastify server on port 3000 (or `process.env.PORT`)
- Two background workers (search reindex, email send) started before listen
- SIGINT/SIGTERM gracefully shuts down workers then app

### Vitest Configuration

**Backend** (`packages/backend/vitest.config.ts`):
- Glob: `**/*.test.ts`
- Timeout: 20s (up from 5s default due to magic-link email flow)
- Global setup: `./test/global-setup.ts` — purges leaked Meili test indexes once per run
- Workers: search/message workers are NOT started in tests; tests drive them explicitly via `reindexOrg()` / `drainOnce()`

**Frontend** (`packages/frontend/vitest.config.ts`):
- Glob: `**/*.test.ts`
- Root: `packages/frontend`

### What is Vamp?

**Vamp** is a custom UI framework/pattern library built for gatherus (not an external package):
- **Location**: `packages/frontend/vamp.ts` (~574 lines)
- **Purpose**: lightweight view/state binding system for vanilla DOM apps
- **Core primitives**:
  - `View<State, Message, Ctx>` interface: each view has `container`, `sync(state)`, `destroy()`
  - `Binder<State>` class: manages reactive bindings (bindText, bindClass, bindVisible, bindStyle, bindAttr, bindChecked, bindValue, bindSlot, bindList, etc.)
  - `show()` / `showKeyed()`: describe child views without mounting (lazy view lifecycle)
  - `RequestStatus<T>`: union type (idle | loading | loaded | error) for async data
  - `PostRenderEventBus`: event system for post-render side effects (scroll, focus, etc.)
- **Design**: Single global dispatch loop in `main.ts`; pages are message handlers that update parent state. Views are stateless renderers that sync DOM on state change. No framework rerenders—only explicit `view.sync()` calls after dispatch.
- **Example**: `mainView.sync(state)` after `update(state, msg, ctx, dispatch)` returns.

### WebSocket Usage

**Location**: `packages/backend/sheets/socket.ts`
- **Package**: `@fastify/websocket@^11.3.0`
- **Endpoint**: `GET /api/sheets/socket` (websocket: true)
- **Purpose**: Real-time collaborative sheet editing
- **Flow**:
  1. Client connects; message listener buffered before first await
  2. Session auth + permission checks (sheet:read, sheet:write, sheet:manage)
  3. `SheetSession` created with transport layer (`send(frame)`, `close(reason)`)
  4. Client messages parsed and routed to `session.receive()`
  5. Server frames JSON-stringified and sent back
  6. Heartbeat ping/pong every 15s (session-leak window)
  7. On close: interval cleared, session closed
- **Wiring**: `registerSheets(app, pool)` in `create-app.ts` calls `registerSheetSocket(app, pool, new Bus())` which registers the websocket route
